sites.cs: DoD MIRTA point OBJECTID 605 'Fallon Range Complex' (usn, status act, state code NV)
f: Childhood leukemia cluster in Churchill County (Fallon): 16 children diagnosed 1997-2002 vs fewer than 2 expected. The CDC-led study (Mar 2001) found no exposure consistent with leukemia risk; urinary tungsten and arsenic were above national values but similar in case and comparison families.

sites.cs: DoD MIRTA point OBJECTID 170 'Makua Mil Reserve' (usa, status act, state code HI)
f: used for live fire and other training for over 80 years (DVIDS 2018)
Known to contain UXO (DVIDS). Army UXO clearance operations continue (controlled detonations, Jan 2026).
2015: two grass-cutting contractors were injured when they set off UXO; the reservation was closed to training and cultural access (DVIDS).

2001 Army-Malama Makua agreement: two cultural-access visits a month and two overnight accesses a year, each escorted by a UXO technician; 3 Aug 2018 court-approved agreement added visits. Over 100 archaeological/historic properties; over 45 threatened and endangered species.

f: U.S. Navy (former); now Kaho'olawe Island Reserve Commission (State of Hawai'i)

UXO remains. Navy UXO Clearance Project ended in 2004: about 75% of the island surface-cleared, 10% (2,647 acres) also cleared to 4 ft, and 25% (6,692 acres) not cleared and unsafe for unescorted access (KIRC history). Surrounding waters not cleared (KIRC FY24/25).
1993 Title X, FY1994 DoD Appropriations Act: conveyance to the State and $400 million for ordnance removal. Deed conveyed 1994; access control returned 11 Nov 2003.

Returned land underwent obstacle-removal (支障除去) measures before hand-over to landowners on 25 Dec 2017 (MOD).
SACO agreement (1996). Returned area became part of the 'Amami-Oshima, Tokunoshima, northern Okinawa and Iriomote' World Natural Heritage site on 26 Jul 2021 (MOD).

f: over 94,000 acres, the UK's largest training area (MOD leaflet)
Live firing for armour, artillery, engineers, infantry and aircraft. MOD warning: 'Unexploded ordnance: do not touch any unidentified object'.
Public access governed by military byelaws; about 68,600 acres reachable by public rights of way, closed when red flags fly; about 50,000 acres in six SSSIs; about 2,300 monuments (550 protected).

sites.n: Cape Wrath Training Area, including Garvie Island air weapons range

Parts designated SSSI, SAC and SPA. The public road to Cape Wrath lighthouse (10 of its 12 miles inside the training area) is closed during live firing.

f: U.S. Air Force (former); site now Hwaseong city parks
US-forces-only bombing range centred on Nong-seom island, 1.6 km off Maehyang-ri. Polluted tidal flats and unprocessed bomb debris remained after closure (Gyeonggi).
11 residents killed and 19 injured during the range's use, including from unexploded munitions (Gyeonggi provincial news).
Site redeveloped as Maehyang-ri Peace Ecology Park (opened Sep 2021) and Kooni Memorial Garden; buildings registered in 2016 as Gyeonggi's first 'excellent architectural asset'.
